summary: TrainMate's migration folder contains one-time tools (not shipped, nothing in src/ depends on them) to move off Lovable Cloud onto a self-owned Supabase + Vercel deployment. Ordered flow: create new Supabase project -> apply schema (`supabase db push` or paste `migration/schema.sql`) -> configure Auth -> `dump.sh` inside Lovable sandbox -> `restore.sh` locally -> `copy-avatars.ts` (storage) -> `resign-avatars.ts` (rewrite signed URLs) -> update .env -> deploy (VERCEL.md). The dump is DATA-ONLY (schema excluded; it's pre-applied). Storage: the `avatars` bucket (private at final schema state; contextual authenticated-only SELECT policy: `(storage.foldername(name))[1] = auth.uid()::text OR can_view_profile(...)`) uses `<userId>/avatar.<ext>` paths (first folder segment = auth user UUID, fixed filename `avatar.<ext>` where ext = original extension). Upload/update/delete policies require `auth.uid()::text = (storage.foldername(name))[1]`. Frontend constructs avatar URLs in `src/hooks/useProfile.ts`: uploadAvatar() builds `fileName = ${user.id}/avatar.${fileExt}`, removes the old object, uploads with upsert, then `createSignedUrl(fileName, 60*60*24*365)` (1-year signed URL) and stores the signed URL into `profiles.avatar_url`. At render, `getAvatarUrl()` strips everything after `?` from the stored URL and appends `?t=${avatarVersion}` (Date.now() cache-buster), which DROPS the signed `token=` param (a gotcha for the private bucket — see notes). Supabase client (`src/integrations/supabase/client.ts`) is created from `VITE_SUPABASE_URL` + `VITE_SUPABASE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY` (anon), auth persisted in localStorage. Chat attachments use a second bucket `chat-attachments` (path `<conversationId>/<uuid>.<ext>`, also 1-year signed URLs via `src/hooks/useChat.tsx uploadAttachment`). The local project is already linked to the target project `trainmate-prod` ref `dfkbtusmnrhzaonouhsk` (region ap-northeast-1, pooler URL `postgresql://postgres.dfkbtusmnrhzaonouhsk@aws-0-ap-northeast-1.pooler.supabase.com:5432/postgres`), and `.env` already points at that new project with a `sb_publishable_...` key. Key constraint: Lovable Cloud does not expose the source `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY` to users, so avatar migration may require a one-time export from Lovable support or user re-upload.
dumpProcess: dump.sh runs INSIDE the Lovable sandbox (or anywhere `PG*` env vars point at the source DB). Requires PGHOST, PGUSER, PGPASSWORD, PGDATABASE (PGPORT defaults to 5432); output defaults to `/mnt/documents/lovable-dump.sql` (override via OUT, `du -h` size printed). It is a DATA-ONLY export: `pg_dump --data-only --no-owner --no-privileges --disable-triggers --column-inserts` with explicit `-t` selection of: `auth.users`, `auth.identities`, `public.profiles`, `public.trains`, `public.unverified_trains`, `public.journeys`, `public.requests`, `public.conversations`, `public.messages`, `public.last_read`, `public.blocked_users`, `public.user_reports`. Crucially there is NO `--schema` and NO `--create`: the new project's schema is expected to already exist (from `supabase db push` / `schema.sql`), and `auth.users`/`auth.identities` rows (including password hashes) are copied so existing users can log in. `--column-inserts` emits explicit-column INSERTs (tolerant of extra/new columns in target auth schema); `--disable-triggers` (ALTER TABLE ... DISABLE TRIGGER ALL around COPYs) suppresses FK/check triggers during load, so FK ordering of tables does not matter on the source. Not exported: storage objects (handled separately by copy-avatars.ts), functions/triggers/policies/schema (pre-applied), the `trains` seed data IS included as it is a real table.
restoreProcess: restore.sh runs locally with psql. Requires NEW_DB_URL (the pooler connection string, e.g. `postgres://postgres.<ref>:<password>@aws-0-<region>.pooler.supabase.com:5432/postgres`) and DUMP (default `/mnt/documents/lovable-dump.sql`; errors if missing). Restores with `psql "$NEW_DB_URL" -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 --single-transaction -f "$DUMP"` — fail-fast on first error and the whole restore wrapped in a single transaction so a failure rolls back cleanly. After the load it prints row counts (auth.users, public.profiles, public.journeys, public.requests, public.conversations, public.messages, public.blocked_users) so the operator can verify nothing was lost against the source. Prerequisite: all migrations applied to the new project first (otherwise FK targets/triggers may not exist). The service-role-ish postgres role in the pooler connection bypasses RLS, so data lands even though the app is RLS-locked. NOTE: restore.sh only counts 7 of the 12 dumped tables and does not verify storage.
avatarMigration: copy-avatars.ts is a `bun run migration/copy-avatars.ts` script using @supabase/supabase-js with TWO service-role clients: oldSb (OLD_SUPABASE_URL + OLD_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY) and newSb (NEW_SUPABASE_URL + NEW_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY). It copies every object in the `avatars` bucket. Exact flow: (1) recursive `listAll()` walks the old bucket — `storage.from('avatars').list(prefix, { limit: 1000, sortBy: { column: 'name', order: 'asc' } })`, recursing into any entry without an `id` (folders), collecting full `path` strings (`<prefix>/<name>`); (2) for each path it `download(path)` from the old bucket, then `upload(path, blob, { upsert: true, contentType: blob.type || undefined })` to the new bucket, preserving the identical object path (`<userId>/avatar.<ext>`), so no path rewriting is needed; (3) per-path try/catch tallies ok/fail and prints `✓/✗ path`, exiting non-zero on any uncaught throw. Both buckets must ALREADY exist (the new `avatars` bucket is created by the migrations; the bucket is private + RLS-protected but service role bypasses RLS for the upload). Service-role keys are used specifically to bypass RLS on both source and destination.
resignProcess: resign-avatars.ts runs `bun run migration/resign-avatars.ts` with only NEW_SUPABASE_URL + NEW_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY (a single service-role client). After copy-avatars.ts, the signed URLs stored in `profiles.avatar_url` still point at the OLD project and would 403. It selects `id, avatar_url` from `profiles` where avatar_url is not null (service role bypasses RLS), then for each profile: (1) derives the storage path from the stored URL with regex `/\/object\/(?:sign|public)\/avatars\/([^?]+)/` (handles both `object/sign/avatars/<path>?token=...` and `object/public/avatars/<path>` forms); (2) fallback if no match — list the user's folder in the NEW bucket (`storage.from('avatars').list(p.id)`) and take the first entry with an `id`, path = `<userId>/<first.name>`; (3) `createSignedUrl(path, 60*60*24*365)` (1 year) against the NEW project; (4) `profiles.update({ avatar_url: signed.signedUrl }).eq('id', p.id)`. Counts ok/missing/failed and prints per-id status. It writes back signed URLs because the bucket is private and the frontend renders signed URLs. This makes the old Lovable URL stale forever — safe, because the Lovable project is left untouched and no code path re-uses old URLs after this.
deploymentNotes: VERCEL.md: standard Vite + React SPA, no Lovable runtime needed. Import repo in Vercel; framework preset `Vite` (auto-detected); build `vite build`; output `dist`; install `npm install` or `bun install`. Add three env vars for Production AND Preview: `VITE_SUPABASE_URL` = `https://<new-ref>.supabase.co`, `VITE_SUPABASE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY` = the new project's anon (publishable) key, `VITE_SUPABASE_PROJECT_ID` = `<new-ref>`. NEVER put the service role key in Vercel — it is only used by the one-off migration scripts. SPA routing handled by the committed `vercel.json` (route `/(.*)` -> /index.html, with passthrough routes for `/assets/(.*)` and static file extensions). Auth config in new Supabase dashboard: Site URL = Vercel domain; Redirect URLs = `https://<domain>/**`, `https://<domain>` (no trailing slash), `https://<project>-*.vercel.app/**` (previews), `http://localhost:5173/**`. Google OAuth: Authorized JS origins = Vercel domain, redirect URI = `https://<new-ref>.supabase.co/auth/v1/callback`, then paste client ID/secret into Supabase Providers->Google. Cutover checklist verifies migrations applied, dump/restore row counts match, copy-avatars + resign-avatars ran (avatar loads from new domain), Vercel deploy, new-user `handle_new_user` trigger creates a profile row, migrated user login, realtime chat, new avatar upload. Rollback = revert the three VITE_* env vars to the old Lovable values and redeploy (Lovable project stays untouched).
envVars: OLD_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY=<lovable service role key, migration-only, may need Lovable support export>
NEW_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY=<new project service role key, migration-only>
notes: Gotchas for migrating avatars/storage: (1) The source service role key is NOT exposed to users by Lovable Cloud — README admits you may need to contact Lovable support for a one-time export, otherwise skip avatar migration and have users re-upload. (2) The `avatars` bucket is PRIVATE in the final schema (set public=false in 20260418102918, never reverted), so objects have no public URL; everything must flow through signed URLs — this is why copy + resign both exist and why useProfile stores 1-year signed URLs. (3) `resign-avatars.ts` must run AFTER `copy-avatars.ts`; if you resign before copy the newly-written URLs 403 until the objects exist. (4) Storage SELECT policy is contextual ("Users can view contextual avatars": folder == auth.uid() OR `can_view_profile(folder_uuid)`); `can_view_profile` is granted only to authenticated (REVOKE'd from anon/public), so the policy works only for logged-in viewers — anonymous `` access to the private bucket is denied even with a stored token stripped. (5) FRONTEND GOTCHA: `getAvatarUrl()` in useProfile.ts does `url.split('?')[0]` then appends `?t=${avatarVersion}` — this DROPS the signed `token=` query param. For a private bucket, `` (used in ProfileMenu.tsx and ViewProfileModal.tsx) requests an UNSIGNED object URL and would 403; meanwhile ProfileModal.tsx renders the raw stored `profile.avatar_url` (token intact). This is inconsistent and should be verified in the app after migration (the resign script's fresh token would also be stripped by getAvatarUrl). If the cache-buster is needed, append `&t=` to the existing query string instead of replacing it. (6) The concatenated `migration/schema.sql` (generated 2026-07-23) does NOT include the newest migration `20260725073436_grant_authenticated_table_privileges.sql` (grants SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE on public schema to authenticated) — use `supabase db push` (there are 31 migrations in supabase/migrations) rather than pasting schema.sql, or regenerate it, or you'll miss the table grants. (7) schema.sql only INSERTs the `avatars` bucket — the `chat-attachments` bucket has RLS policies but NO `storage.buckets` INSERT anywhere, so it must be created manually on the new project or chat attachment uploads fail (and copy-avatars.ts only handles `avatars`, not chat attachments). (8) `--disable-triggers` on pg_dump emits ALTER TABLE ... DISABLE TRIGGER ALL, which needs elevated privileges on the source; on managed Lovable/Supabase this may be rejected — if so, drop that flag (FK ordering is handled because restore targets pre-existing schema; without it, rely on FK enforcement or reorder). (9) Restore uses the TRANSACTION pooler URL, not the session pooler — with `--single-transaction` it is fine, but don't use `pgbouncer=true` session mode for multi-statement loads. (10) `restore.sh` verification only counts 7 of the 12 tables; sanity-check `last_read`, `user_reports`, `unverified_trains`, `trains`, `auth.identities` manually. (11) `auth.users` data-only insert into a fresh project can fail if the target auth schema gained NOT-NULL columns without defaults or if identities have conflicts; check for partial restore before cutover. (12) The `.temp/linked-project.json`, `project-ref`, and `pooler-url` show the repo is already linked to `trainmate-prod` (dfkbtusmnrhzaonouhsk, ap-northeast-1) and `.env` already uses `VITE_SUPABASE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY` = `sb_publishable_...` (new publishable-key format, not legacy anon JWT) — these migration steps appear already executed for this project.
